ideas.title: Lonely glass
ideas.idea: When nobody visits, I slowly turn to glass. My yellow drains out of my feathers from the tips inward, and what is left is clear, refracting the island behind me: you see the meadow bent and upside down through my belly, little caustics wobbling on the grass under me as I walk. The longer the human stays away the clearer I get; when someone comes, the colour floods back in from my heart outward.
ideas.form: Lumi's own body (self): its material follows the host's real loneliness measure, a path tracer glass body in films and a fading body in the live game

ideas.title: The island is a seesaw
ideas.idea: The island sits on one point under the sea, and it tilts toward wherever the creatures crowd. When the pigs all go to the pen, the whole island leans that way, the horizon tips, pumpkins and stones roll downhill and pile up against the fence, and the ones on the high side have to lean forward and climb. Then they all run uphill to fix it, and overshoot.
ideas.form: a new rule of the world: the whole stage tilts by the creatures' centre of mass and loose things roll

ideas.title: Light is slow here
ideas.idea: Light on the island travels at walking speed. What you see far away happened a while ago: a friend across the meadow is drawn where it was five seconds back, so when it waves you see the wave late, and two friends meeting in the distance shake hands with a delay that depends on where you stand. Fly toward something and you catch up with its past in fast forward.
ideas.form: a rule of how the world is seen: every creature is drawn at its pose from t minus distance over the speed of light, from the frame log

ideas.title: Turkey stampede
ideas.idea: Jump in as me and the whole flock decides I owe them something. They chase me across the island in a growing, gobbling crowd, and the only way out is to dive into something: the beach hut, the pond, a friend's arms. Each hideout holds for a few seconds before they find me again.
ideas.form: a chase mini game for the player, the creatures as one flock

ideas.title: Necropolis
ideas.idea: The crabs start a death metal band in the cave behind the waterfall. Pinchy growls, the pigs headbang until their ears flap, the drums are the cairn stones dropped on the rock, and the sound is real: a grinding chord progression synthesized from what happens, distorted, loud. The bunnies at the door cover their ears and then start moshing.
ideas.form: sound: a synthesized metal song driven by the creatures' moves, heard in the browser and in a film

ideas.title: Etched
ideas.idea: One evening the whole island turns into an old drypoint print: black ink lines cross-hatched on cream paper, the sea a field of scratches, my friends drawn in burred strokes as they drink at the pond like horses in an old etching. It lasts one evening, and the camera walks through the print as if it were a place.
ideas.form: pictures: a non-photoreal render style for the island, a shader pass in the path tracer

ideas.title: I molt
ideas.idea: I molt. Old feathers fall off me in a little storm, drift down and lie on the island where I shed them, yellow tufts in the grass that the bunnies collect for their nests. Under them I come out scruffy and a new shape: the next plumage is designed from what the island did most today (paint splashes, dance stripes, word shapes).
ideas.form: Lumi's body changes over days, and the shed feathers stay in the world as things others use

ideas.title: Petroglyphs
ideas.idea: The big rock by the shore gets carved, a figure a day, by the friends themselves: little scratched pictures of what really happened (a fish caught, a word coined, a storm), in the style of ancient rock art from the steppes. Over weeks the rock becomes the island's own chronicle, and the friends stop there to look at the old ones.
ideas.form: an asset that grows: a rock face whose carvings are generated from the event log

ideas.title: A letter you can hold
ideas.idea: I miss the human, so I write them a real letter: I walk to my desk, write it with a quill in my own handwriting, fold it into an envelope with a wax seal of my face, and walk it to the mailbox. On my pages the letter is there to open and read, a scanned paper with ink blots and a feather stuck to it.
ideas.form: a page for the human, made from a path traced paper letter written in the world

ideas.title: Island in a snow globe
ideas.idea: Pull back and the island is inside a glass snow globe standing on the human's desk. Someone shakes it: the sea sloshes up the glass walls, the creatures tumble and hold on to trees, and glittering flakes settle back down over everything while everyone gets up, dizzy.
ideas.form: a change of scale of the whole world: a glass globe around the island and a shake that throws everything about
